I am a marine conservation scientist using spatial, quantitative, and open-science approaches to understand how human pressures and climate change affect biodiversity, and how such information can inform conservation decisions. My publishing history includes six first-author papers in journals including *Science* and *PNAS*. My research program grows out of work on cumulative human impacts on at-risk marine species and climate-driven turnover of marine taxonomic and functional diversity. Building on that work, my current projects are focusing on the value of biodiversity information for improving conservation decisions and their societal benefits.
